solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruler's repressing over half of region

indicators.note: to repress is to hold down, so the ruler's name holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a prince is a ruler; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word over means its first two letters only

explanation.surface: A monarch is clamping down on a large part of their territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler's repressing' reads as a ruler's act of oppression, but the 's means 'is': the ruler is holding down half of 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative division or area of a country.

clue.text: Yorkshire town's darling gets VIP treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire; the 's is a possessive joining it to the next word
a pet is a darling, a favourite person

explanation.surface: A local favourite from a northern English town is given celebrity handling.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson carpet for arrivals is the classic welcome for important guests, so the phrase means special honour.

clue.text: Wine's absorbed effectively opening blood vessels

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the wine word takes in the letter

parts.note: vin is French for wine, with the S of the 's kept

indicators.note: the opening of the word effectively is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wine soaks quickly into the bloodstream once it gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes E from 'effectively', and 'absorbed' puts it inside VINS (VIN, French wine, plus the S of 's).
explanation.definitionFit: Veins are the vessels that carry blood back to the heart.

clue.text: Man's heading off to get clobber for disco

indicators.note: with the heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a knight is a man in chess; the 's is read as 'has'
to clobber is to hit, as with a club

explanation.surface: A man heads out to pick up some clothes for a night of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' is British slang for clothes, but here it is the verb 'hit'. 'heading off' drops the K of KNIGHT to leave NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a venue for dancing to recorded music late into the evening.

clue.text: Abstains from upside down pudding most of school's tucked into

indicators.note: the school abbreviation is pushed inside the other letters
in a down clue, upside down means the letters are read from bottom to top
most of the word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: pudding in Britain is the sweet course of a meal
SCH is a standard abbreviation for school; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an upside-down pudding that most of the school is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down pudding' looks like a dessert, but 'most of' trims the sweet to SWEE and 'upside down' makes EEWS before the school letters go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately avoid or shun it.

clue.text: Observes endless wonder in children's plaything

parts.note: to observe is to see

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Someone watches, amazed, as children play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts AWE down to AW.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank that two children ride up and down.

clue.text: Son has desire to be posh

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A boy wants to be upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for smart, fashionable or elegant.

clue.text: Sixteen converts taking on church's way of life

indicators.note: converts tells us to change the form of the letters of sixteen

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England; the 's is a possessive

explanation.surface: Sixteen converts join a church and take on its whole way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers, but it signals rearranging SIXTEEN into EXISTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence can mean a particular manner of living, as in a quiet existence.

clue.text: Arizona river's deep blue

parts.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Arizona
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A river in Arizona is a deep blue colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the bright, deep blue colour of a clear sky.

clue.text: Journalist's going to reject nothing to reach border

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: rejecting the zero means throwing it out of the word going

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A reporter gives up on nothing in order to reach the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reject' throws the O out of GOING, which leaves GING.
explanation.definitionFit: Edging is a decorative strip or trim running along the edge of something.

clue.text: Credit one quite original review

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: original in the sense of novel or new-made: the letters of quite are formed afresh

explanation.surface: Praise for a fairly original appraisal of some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' looks like praise for the review, but it signals rearranging QUITE into TIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A critique is a detailed critical assessment of a work, like a review.

clue.text: Brief tumble with Henry on settee broke dentures

indicators.note: in an across clue, Henry placed on the settee letters comes after them
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a tumble is a fall

indicators.note: broke shows the letters of settee are smashed into a new order

parts.note: H is the SI symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A quick fall on to a sofa, with Henry aboard, smashes someone's dentures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts FALL to FAL, and 'broke' rearranges SETTEE into SETEET.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth are artificial replacements for natural ones, which is what dentures are.

clue.text: Hiker turned back during long walk …

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
during says the answer lies within the clue words that come before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A walker turns around partway through a long hike.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'during long walk' as the definition, but 'during' is the signal for letters lying inside 'Hiker turned' (KERT), which 'back' turns around. The definition is just 'long walk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey on foot.

clue.text: … getting hot and sick on high ascent

parts.note: on high means up, raised
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A climber continuing a hike, feverish and nauseous as they go higher.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the hiker of the previous one; it has no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, uphill means an upward slope or climb.

clue.text: Possessed trendy robe by Spain's leading designer

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a habit is a monk's or nun's robe
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España); the 's is a possessive

indicators.note: the leading letter of designer is its first

explanation.surface: A fashionable robe was owned by Spain's top fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' looks like 'owned', but here it means occupied by a spirit, as in a house inhabited by ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunted house is occupied by a spirit, so 'possessed' and 'dwelt in' share the sense of being occupied.

clue.text: Bookmaker's pursuing final bets for good runner

indicators.note: something pursuing comes after, so the printer word follows the letter
final picks the last letter of bets

parts.note: a printer makes books; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A bookie chases late wagers on a fast racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a bookie taking bets, but here it is someone who makes books: a PRINTER. 'final' picks the S of 'bets', and 'pursuing' puts PRINTER after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is an athlete or animal that runs fast over short distances.

clue.text: RAF, hosting princess on round tour, cut time in wireless station

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the letters of RAF take others within them

parts.note: Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales
O is round in shape

indicators.note: cut says the word tour loses the letter for time

explanation.surface: The air force entertains a princess on a royal tour that is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio 4 is the BBC's main speech radio station in the UK; 'wireless' is the old British word for radio. The first part builds RADIOF, and 'cut' leaves OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio 4 is a BBC broadcasting channel, so it is a station heard on the radio set.

clue.text: Sick, no question, when regularly spoiled with a piece of cake

indicators.note: no says the question abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: queasy means sick, nauseous
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of spoiled

explanation.surface: Someone sick without question, after a regular diet of being spoiled with cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes QU out of QUEASY to leave EASY. 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'spoiled' (P, I, E).
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very simple to do.

clue.text: A teetotaller chap gets stick when buying drinks

parts.note: TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
he is a chap, a man
a bar is a stick, a rod

explanation.surface: A non-drinking man is given a hard time when it's his round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks are ordered across the counter of a pub, so the phrase describes where buying takes place.

clue.text: Take top off container and hold it up to get wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding the letters up makes them read from bottom to top
taking the top off means removing the first letter

parts.note: a canister is a container

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a vessel and raising it to get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take top off' turns CANISTER into ANISTER, and 'hold it up' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Smart to bandage wound with yarrow initially

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of yarrow

explanation.surface: First-aid advice: bind a cut with the herb yarrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like a separate injury, but 'bandage wound' together means DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and elegant rather than casual.

clue.text: Wedge key behind post at side of door

indicators.note: the key comes behind, so it goes after the other piece

parts.note: to jam something is to wedge it
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Wedging a key behind a doorpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side piece of a doorway or window frame.

clue.text: Sleepless and feeble with no energy in hospital department

indicators.note: in says the trimmed weak word sits inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: A&E is the British accident and emergency department

indicators.note: with no says the energy letter is taken out

parts.note: weak means feeble
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An exhausted, insomniac patient lies in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (accident and emergency) is the UK's term for the hospital emergency room. 'with no' drops the E of 'feeble' (WEAK), and 'in' puts the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sleepless means not sleeping, and so being conscious and alert.

clue.text: Scheme has one Scottish family importing bubbly Pinot

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the family takes other letters inside it

parts.note: a clan is a Scottish family group

indicators.note: bubbly shows the letters of pinot fizzing into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish family's plan includes bringing in sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like a description of the wine, but it rearranges the grape name into TIONP.
explanation.definitionFit: An action plan is a detailed strategy setting out the steps to reach a goal.

clue.text: Nowadays old man gets upset and tense with change

parts.note: AD (Anno Domini) marks the present era

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a father, an old man
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: These days an elderly man becomes upset and stressed by change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' turns PA into AP; 'tense' looks like an emotion but is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to adjust or modify, making something different to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Walked up and down with cigarette, gutted and gripped by writer's block

indicators.note: something gripped by another sits inside it

parts.note: a pad is a block of writing paper

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone smoking anxiously, devastated and stuck with writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' looks like the creative condition but is a notepad, and 'gutted' looks like 'devastated' but empties the cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To pace is to walk back and forth repeatedly, often when anxious.

clue.text: Gone with sheep and pig heart to make meat product

parts.note: something gone is past
a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: the heart of pig is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for using sheep and a pig's heart to make a meaty deli product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' looks like offal, but it picks the I from the middle of 'pig'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned smoked beef, a classic delicatessen meat.

clue.text: Take possession of old college trophy on last day

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: A college team holds on to an old trophy on the final day.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy territory or a building is to seize and hold it.

clue.text: Some returning Wapiti deer go back over again

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few elk heading home retrace their route.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit text is to revise it once more, going through the copy a second time.

clue.text: Cut down crossing between Austria and Germany

indicators.note: the crossing sits between the two country codes

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: A bridge on the Austrian-German border has been demolished.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text has been shortened or condensed.
